questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of net cash flow?
options: Total cash inflows minus total cash outflows for a period
Revenue minus costs for a period
The cash held at the end of a period
Profit after tax
questions.why: Net cash flow measures the movement of cash in a period. Adding it to the opening balance gives the closing balance.
whyNot: That is profit, which is a different measure.
That is the closing balance.
Profit after tax is an accounting measure, not a cash movement.

questions.stem: Opening balance is $4,000 and net cash flow is negative $500. What is the closing balance?
options: negative $4,500
questions.why: Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow = 4,000 + (-500) = $3,500.
whyNot: This adds $500 instead of subtracting it.
That is the net cash flow figure, not the balance.
This subtracts the opening balance as well.

questions.stem: In a cash flow forecast, this month's closing balance becomes:
options: next month's opening balance
next month's net cash flow
next month's total inflows
the profit for the month
questions.why: The carry-forward is the whole point of the forecast, and it is where most marks are lost in a Calculate question.
whyNot: Net cash flow is calculated from that month's own inflows and outflows.
Inflows are the cash received in the month.
A cash flow forecast does not show profit at all.

questions.stem: Why can a profitable business run out of cash?
options: Customers may pay long after the sale is recorded as revenue
Profit is always lower than cash
Profitable businesses never need finance
Cash and profit are the same thing
questions.why: A sale becomes revenue when the goods go out and cash when the customer pays, perhaps 60 days later. Meanwhile wages and suppliers still have to be paid. This is the most important distinction in WBS12.
whyNot: Either can be higher. It depends on timing and on non-cash items.
Profitable businesses frequently need finance to bridge timing gaps.
They are different, and confusing them is the most heavily penalised error in this unit.

questions.stem: Which of the following appears in a cash flow forecast but not as a cost in the income statement?
options: The capital repayment element of a loan
Depreciation
Wages
Rent
questions.why: Repaying the capital is a cash outflow but not an expense; only the interest is a cost. Depreciation is the mirror image: a cost with no cash movement.
whyNot: Depreciation is a cost with no cash effect, so it appears in the income statement and NOT in the cash flow forecast.
Wages appear in both.
Rent appears in both.

questions.stem: Which of the following would NOT appear in a cash flow forecast?
options: Depreciation
A loan repayment
Cash from sales
Rent paid
questions.why: Depreciation involves no movement of cash. It spreads the cost of an asset over its life in the income statement, and the cash left when the asset was bought.
whyNot: A loan repayment is a real cash outflow.
Cash from sales is the main inflow.
Rent paid is a cash outflow.

questions.stem: A business has a negative closing balance forecast for one month only, caused by a customer paying late. How should this be described?
options: A timing problem, which short-term finance can bridge
A viability problem, meaning the business model does not work
Insolvency, so the business must close
Evidence the business is unprofitable
questions.why: Distinguishing a timing problem from a viability problem is one of the strongest evaluation moves on this topic. A one-month gap from late payment is very different from costs permanently exceeding revenue.
whyNot: Viability means costs exceed revenue over time, which is not what is described.
A forecast shortfall is a warning, and arranging an overdraft in advance avoids it.
Nothing here suggests the business is unprofitable.

questions.stem: Which action would speed up cash inflows?
options: Offering customers a discount for early payment
Negotiating longer credit terms with suppliers
Leasing equipment rather than buying it
Delaying payment of the electricity bill
questions.why: Early-payment discounts bring cash in sooner. The cost is the discount given, so like every cash flow remedy it has a price.
whyNot: That slows outflows, which also helps, but it is not an inflow.
Leasing avoids a large outflow; it does not accelerate an inflow.
Also slowing an outflow, and risky.

questions.stem: Why is an annual cash flow figure of limited use to a seasonal business?
options: It hides the months when revenue is low but fixed costs still have to be paid
Annual figures cannot be calculated
Seasonal businesses have no cash flow
Annual figures always understate cash
questions.why: A guesthouse can be comfortably cash positive across the year and unable to pay August's wages. Annual profit does not pay August's wages, which is why the forecast must be monthly.
whyNot: They can be, and that is the problem: the average conceals the trough.
They have highly variable cash flow, which is exactly the issue.
An annual total neither over nor understates; it conceals the distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation of a cash flow forecast?
options: It is built on estimates, especially of sales, which may be wrong
It cannot show negative balances
It cannot be shown to a bank
It must be prepared annually by law
questions.why: One optimistic sales assumption invalidates the rest, and customers paying later than assumed can wreck it. It is a planning tool, not a prediction.
whyNot: Negative balances are exactly what it is designed to reveal.
Showing it to a lender is one of its main uses.
There is no such legal requirement for most businesses.

questions.stem: What is the cost of using factoring to improve cash flow?
options: The business receives less than the full value of its invoices
The business must give up equity
Interest rates on all its loans rise
It loses limited liability
questions.why: Factoring gets cash for invoices now, and the factor takes a fee, so the business receives less than the invoice value. Every cash flow remedy has a price, and naming it is how you earn the evaluation mark.
whyNot: No ownership is given up in factoring.
Factoring does not change existing loan terms.
Legal form and liability are unaffected.
